arxiv-2106-14112.title: Time-Series Representation Learning via Temporal and Contextual Contrasting
arxiv-2106-14112.creator: Emadeldeen Eldele, Mohamed Ragab, Zhenghua Chen, Min Wu, Chee Keong Kwoh, Xiaoli Li, Cuntai Guan
arxiv-2106-14112.description: Abstract Learning decent representations from unlabeled time-series data with temporal dynamics is a very challenging task. In this paper, we propose an unsupervised T ime- S eries representation learning framework via T emporal and C ontextual C ontrasting ( TS-TCC ), to learn time-series representation from unlabeled data.

arxiv-2111-08892.title: SAPNet: Segmentation-Aware Progressive Network for Perceptual Contrastive Deraining
arxiv-2111-08892.creator: Shen Zheng, Changjie Lu, Yuxiong Wu, Gaurav Gupta
arxiv-2111-08892.description: Abstract Deep learning algorithms have recently achieved promising deraining performances on both the natural and synthetic rainy datasets. As an essential low-level pre-processing stage, a deraining network should clear the rain streaks and preserve the fine semantic details. However, most existing methods only consider low-level image restoration. That limits their performances at high-level tasks requiring precise semantic information.

arxiv-2203-10316.title: Learning to Reason Deductively: Math Word Problem Solving as Complex Relation Extraction
arxiv-2203-10316.creator: Zhanming Jie, Jierui Li, Wei Lu
arxiv-2203-10316.description: Abstract Solving math word problems requires deductive reasoning over the quantities in the text. Various recent research efforts mostly relied on sequence-to-sequence or sequence-to-tree models to generate mathematical expressions without explicitly performing relational reasoning between quantities in the given context. While empirically effective, such approaches typically do not provide explanations for the generated expressions.

arxiv-2206-09535.title: Characterizing Human Actions in the Digital Platform by Temporal Context
arxiv-2206-09535.creator: Akira Matsui, Emilio Ferrara
arxiv-2206-09535.description: Abstract Recent advances in digital platforms generate rich, high‑dimensional logs of human behavior, and machine learning models have helped social scientists explain knowledge accumulation, communication, and information diffusion. Such models, however, almost always treat behavior as sequences of actions, abstracting the inter‑temporal information among actions.

arxiv-2211-07818.title: AgileAvatar: Stylized 3D Avatar Creation via Cascaded Domain Bridging 384 Thanks: Authors’ email addresses: Shen Sang: shen.sang@bytedance.com; Tiancheng Zhi: tiancheng.zhi@bytedance.com; Guoxian Song: guoxiansong@bytedance.com; Minghao Liu: mliu40@ucsc.edu; Chunpong Lai: chunpong.lai@bytedance.com;
arxiv-2211-07818.creator: Shen Sang, Tiancheng Zhi, Guoxian Song, Minghao Liu, Chunpong Lai, Jing Liu, Xiang Wen, James Davis, Linjie Luo
arxiv-2211-07818.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shen Sang, Tiancheng Zhi, Guoxian Song, Minghao Liu, Chunpong Lai, Jing Liu, Xiang Wen, James Davis, Linjie Luo. Stylized 3D avatars have become increasingly prominent in our modern life. Creating these avatars manually usually involves laborious selection and adjustment of continuous and discrete parameters and is time-consuming for average users. Self-supervised approaches to automatically create 3D avatars from user selfies promise high quality with little annotation cost but fall short in application to stylized avatars due to a large style domain gap.

arxiv-2212-05525.title: Extending TrOCR for Text Localization-Free OCR of Full-Page Scanned Receipt Images
arxiv-2212-05525.creator: Hongkuan Zhang 1 , Edward Whittaker 2 , Ikuo Kitagishi 3 1 Nagoya University 2 K.K. Best Path Research 3 Money Forward, Inc
arxiv-2212-05525.description: Abstract Digitization of scanned receipts aims to extract text from receipt images and save it into structured documents. This is usually split into two sub-tasks: text localization and optical character recognition (OCR). Most existing OCR models only focus on the cropped text instance images, which require the bounding box information provided by a text region detection model.

arxiv-2305-01865.title: Collective Lamb Shift and Modified Linewidth of An Interacting Atomic Gas
arxiv-2305-01865.creator: Hanzhen Ma, Susanne F. Yelin
arxiv-2305-01865.description: Abstract Finding a comprehensive and general description of the collective Lamb shift and cooperative broadening in a radiatively interacting system is a long-standing open question. Both energy levels and linewidth of individual atoms are modified by the exchange of real and virtual photons making up the dipole-dipole interaction.

arxiv-2312-03180.title: Image reconstructions using sparse dictionary representations and implicit, non-negative mappings
arxiv-2312-03180.creator: Elizabeth Newman, Jack Michael Solomon, Matthias Chung
arxiv-2312-03180.description: Abstract Many imaging science tasks can be modeled as a discrete linear inverse problem. Solving linear inverse problems is often challenging, with ill-conditioned operators and potentially non-unique solutions. Embedding prior knowledge, such as smoothness, into the solution can overcome these challenges.

pmc-10699020.title: Atypical antipsychotic use does not impact weight gain for individuals with extreme anorexia nervosa: a retrospective case–control study
pmc-10699020.creator: Maryrose Bauschka, Ashlie Watters, Dan Blalock, Asma Farooq, Philip Mehler, Dennis Gibson
pmc-10699020.description: BackgroundThere are no U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved medications for the treatment of anorexia nervosa (AN). Various medication classes have been evaluated for benefits in this population, including antipsychotics. Studies focused on use of antipsychotics for assistance with weight restoration in AN produced conflicting results.

pmc-11489314.title: Evaluating the benefits of urban green infrastructure: Methods, indicators, and gaps
pmc-11489314.creator: Soheila Khalili, Prashant Kumar, Laurence Jones
pmc-11489314.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Green infrastructure (GI) offers a promising solution for mitigating the adverse effects of climate change, but evaluating its effectiveness necessitates a comprehensive understanding of how that has been quantified in the literature. This study aims to review the methods (monitoring, remote sensing, and modelling) employed to assess the effectiveness of GI in urban areas for three ecosystem services: heat mitigation (cooling of air temperature), thermal comfort control, and air quality mitigation.

pmc-12562036.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in the Era of Climate Change: Why We Should All Embrace and Integrate the One Health Approach in Clinical Practice?
pmc-12562036.creator: Dimitris C Kounatidis, Apostolos Evangelopoulos, Eleni V Geladari, Angelos A Evangelopoulos, Andreas Adamou, Sofia Kargioti, Charalampia V Geladari, Maria Dalamaga, Vasileios Sevastianos, Natalia G Vallianou, Carlos M Franco
pmc-12562036.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR), recognized as one of the top ten global public health threats, is projected to cause around 10 million deaths annually by 2050. This trajectory can be averted by adopting the One Health Approach, which acknowledges the interconnection between human, animal, and environmental health.

pmc-12802266.title: Exploring the toxicological impact of DEHP exposure on colorectal cancer through network toxicology, machine learning and bioinformatics analysis
pmc-12802266.creator: Ling Wang, Yuning Qin, Wenbin Fan
pmc-12802266.description: ObjectiveColorectal cancer (CRC) ranks among the most prevalent malignant tumors, yet its underlying mechanisms remain not fully understood. The role of environmental factors is critical in its development and progression. Di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP), a widespread environmental contaminant, poses significant hazards to human health.

pmc-13044247.title: The intracellular inositol (pyro)phosphate receptor AtSPX1 reciprocally binds to P1BS DNA
pmc-13044247.creator: Hayley L. Whitfield, Megan Gilmartin, Andrew M. Riley, Megan L. Shipton, Barry V. L. Potter, Andrew M. Hemmings, Charles A. Brearley
pmc-13044247.description: The response of plants to phosphate starvation engages PHR (CC-MYB-PHOSPHATE STARVATION RESPONSE) transcription factors that bind to P1BS (GNATATNC) promoter elements of phosphate-starvation induced (PSI) genes. The encoded proteins include single-domain SPX (SYG1/Pho81/XPR1) proteins. SPX proteins bind PHR proteins. Current models of SPX1: PHR interaction define only a high-phosphate role for SPX1, as an inositol (pyro)phosphate-dependent negative regulator of PHR.

pmc-13096763.title: Binding Mode Analysis of Antifouling Compounds Targeting Tyrosinase and Acetylcholinesterase by Saturation Transfer Difference NMR Spectroscopy
pmc-13096763.creator: Ana Sara Gomes, Mariana Andrade, Diana I S P Resende, Sara M Cravo, Emília Sousa, Marta Correia‐da‐Silva
pmc-13096763.description: Ecofriendly and sustainable antifouling (AF) compounds are required to replace toxic additives in maritime AF coatings. Our group has developed synthetic AF compounds with anti‐settlement activity toward Mytilus galloprovincialis mussel with nontoxic properties against this target organism. Some compounds have shown to be capable of modulating the activity of key enzymes involved in mussel settlement, namely, tyrosinase and acetylcholinesterase (AChE).
